context: Identify tables whose job is identifying a specific run and route their labels through runIdentity. Leave the dense matrix alone. Separately, give the eligibility asterisk an inline legend wherever it appears, since it is currently unexplained.
description:
src/lib/runIdentity.ts already escalates a run label through version, date, scale, deployment, trust and ID (runIdentity.ts:232-270). RankTable already consumes it. Index tables that show a bare version can produce indistinguishable rows.

Scoping correction from review: QueryHeatmap's dense matrix is NOT a fork of runIdentity - its compact row label is a deliberate density contract (QueryHeatmap.tsx:694-708), and the trailing asterisk marks ranking eligibility, not identity. Applying the escalating formatter there would be the wrong grain. This item targets index and list tables only.

anti_patterns.dont: apply the escalating identity formatter to QueryHeatmap's dense grid
anti_patterns.instead: restrict to index and list tables
anti_patterns.why: the dense grid trades identity detail for column density on purpose

anti_patterns.instead: make worktree-create BRANCH=... WORKTREE_PATH=... then make agent-write-preflight
anti_patterns.why: AGENTS.md makes the primary clone read-only for agents

anti_patterns.dont: invent a new date-plus-short-id label format
anti_patterns.why: a parallel format reinvents and weakens the existing one

preserves.behavior: QueryHeatmap's density contract and compact row labels

verifications.expected: typecheck clean; all vitest suites pass

work_units.summary: Route index-table row labels through runIdentity
